nodes.name: Theorem 2.1: $\Pr\qty[\tau_{\mathrm{cons}}>\frac{C\log n}{\gamma_0}]\leq O(n^{-1})$
nodes.statement:
The consensus time of 3-Majority starting from any initial configuration provided that $\gamma_0 \ge \frac{C\log n}{\sqrt{n}}$ for a sufficiently large constant $C>0$ is $O\qty(\frac{\log n}{\gamma_0})$ with high probability.

  Similarly, the consensus time of 2-Choices starting from any initial configuration provided that $\gamma_0 \ge \frac{C(\log n)^2}{n}$ for a sufficiently large constant $C>0$ is $O\qty(\frac{\log n}{\gamma_0})$ with high probability.

nodes.name: Theorem 2.6: Plurality If $\alpha_0(1)\geq \alpha_0(j)+C\sqrt{\log n/n}$ for $\forall j\neq 1$…
nodes.statement:
Let $C>0$ be a sufficiently large constant.
    Consider 3-Majority starting with any initial configuration such that
    $\gamma_0\geq \frac{C\log n}{\sqrt{n}}$ and $\alpha_0(1)-\alpha_0(j)\geq C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}$ for all $j\neq 1$.
    Then, for some $T=O\qty(\frac{\log n}{\gamma_0})$, we have $\alpha_T(1)=1$ with high probability.

    Similarly, consider 2-Choices starting with any initial configuration such that $\gamma_0\geq \frac{C(\log n)^2}{n}$ and $\alpha_0(1)-\alpha_0(j)\geq C\sqrt{\frac{\alpha_0(1)\log n}{n}}$ for all $j\neq 1$.
    Then, for some $T=O\qty(\frac{\log n}{\gamma_0})$, we have $\alpha_T(1)=1$ with high probability.

nodes.statement:
Let $ i,j $ be distinct opinions that are not weak at round $ 0 $.
    Consider the stopping time $\tau^{\mathrm{weak}}_j $ defined in 4.4 and let $c^{\mathrm{weak}}=1/10$.
    Then, we have the following:
    We have the following:
\begin{enumerate}
  
        \item 
        Consider 3-Majority. 
        Suppose $\alpha_0(i)- \alpha_0(j)\geq C\sqrt{\frac{\log n}{n}}$ and 
        $\gamma_0\geq \frac{C\log n}{\sqrt{n}}$ for a sufficiently large constant $C>0$.
        Then,
        \[
        \Pr\qty[\tau^{\mathrm{weak}}_j>\frac{C\log n}{\gamma_0}]\leq O(n^{-10}).
        \]
        \item 
        Consider 2-Choices. 
        Suppose $\alpha_0(i)- \alpha_0(j)\geq C\sqrt{\frac{\alpha_0(i)\log n}{n}}$ and 
        $\gamma_0\geq \frac{(C\log n)^2}{n}$ for a sufficiently large constant $C>0.$
        Then,
        \[
        \Pr\qty[\tau^{\mathrm{weak}}_j>\frac{C\log n}{\gamma_0}]\leq O(n^{-10}).
        \]
\end{enumerate}

  Then, we have

Lemma 5.7, Lemma 5.8, Lemma 5.9: OST $\delta_t^2$
nodes.statement:
Let $ i,j $ be distinct opinions.
    Consider the stopping times $ \tau^{\mathrm{weak}}_i,\tau^{\mathrm{weak}}_j,\tau^{\downarrow}_i,\tau^{\downarrow}_j $ defined in 4.4.
    Let $\tau\mathrel{\mathop:}= \min\{\tau^{\mathrm{weak}}_i,\tau^{\mathrm{weak}}_j,\tau^{\downarrow}_i,\tau^{\downarrow}_j\}$.
    Let $C_{\mbox{\tiny4.6}}= 1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2(1-c^{\mathrm{weak}})}}$ be a positive constant defined in 4.6.
    
    
    
    
    Then, we have
    \[
    \mathbb{E}[\tau]\leq \frac{\mathbb{E}\qty[\delta_\tau(i,j)^2]}{s_{\mbox{\tiny5.7}}},
    \]
    where
    \begin{align*}
    s_{\mbox{\tiny5.7}}=
    \begin{cases*}
         C_{\mbox{\tiny4.6}}^3(1-c^{\downarrow}_\alpha)\frac{\max\{\alpha_0(i),\alpha_0(j)\}}{n}& \text{for 3-Majority},\\
         C_{\mbox{\tiny4.6}}^2(1-c^{\downarrow}_\alpha)^2\frac{\max\{\alpha_0(i),\alpha_0(j)\}^2}{n}& \text{for 2-Choices}
    \end{cases*}.
    
    \end{align*}

Let $ i,j $ be distinct opinions.
    Consider the stopping times 
    defined in 4.4 and let $\tau=\min\{\tau^{+}_\delta,\tau^{\mathrm{weak}}_i,\tau^{\mathrm{weak}}_j,\tau^{\uparrow}_i,\tau^{\uparrow}_j,\tau^{\downarrow}_i,\tau^{\downarrow}_j\}$.
    Let $s_{\mbox{\tiny5.7}}$ be a parameter defined in 5.7 and
    let $C_{\mbox{\tiny4.6}}= 1-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2(1-c^{\mathrm{weak}})}}$ be a positive constant defined in 4.6.
    Let $C_{\delta}$ be a positive constant defined by
    \begin{align*}
        C_{\delta}=
        \begin{cases*}
            \frac{2(1+c^{\uparrow}_\alpha)}{C_{\mbox{\tiny4.6}}^3(1-c^{\downarrow}_\alpha)}& \text{for 3-Majority}\\
            \frac{2(1+c^{\uparrow}_\alpha)^2(3-2c^{\mathrm{weak}})}{C_{\mbox{\tiny4.6}}^2(1-c^{\downarrow}_\alpha)^2(1-c^{\mathrm{weak}})}& \text{for 2-Choices}.
        \end{cases*}
        
    \end{align*}
    Let $C_{\mbox{\tiny5.8}}\geq C_{\delta}/2>0$ be a sufficiently large constant such that $x\exp(-\frac{2}{C_{\delta}}x)\leq \frac{1}{100}$ holds for all $x\geq C_{\mbox{\tiny5.8}}$.
    
    Suppose that $x_{\delta}\geq \frac{2\log n}{n}$ and $\frac{x_{\delta}^2}{s_{\mbox{\tiny5.7}}}\geq C_{\mbox{\tiny5.8}}$ hold.
   
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
        
    
    Then, 
    \begin{align*}
    
    \mathbb{E}[\delta_\tau(i,j)^2]\leq 16x_{\delta}^2+\frac{s_{\mbox{\tiny5.7}}}{2}\mathbb{E}[\tau].
    \end{align*}

Let $ i,j $ be distinct opinions.
    Consider the stopping times $\tau^{+}_\delta,\tau^{\mathrm{weak}}_i,\tau^{\mathrm{weak}}_j$ defined in 4.4.
    Let $\tau=\min\{\tau^{+}_\delta,\tau^{\mathrm{weak}}_i,\tau^{\mathrm{weak}}_j\}$
    and $s_{\mbox{\tiny5.7}}$ be a positive parameter defined in 5.7.
    Suppose $\frac{x_{\delta}^2}{s_{\mbox{\tiny5.7}}}\leq C$ for some positive constant $C>0$.
    
    
    
    
    Then, $\Pr\qty[\tau>1]\leq 1-c$ holds for some positive constant $c\in (0,1)$.
